'''''Snatch''''' is a [[Crime fiction|crime]] [[comedy-drama]] television series based on the [[Snatch (film)|film of the same name]], and that premiered on March 16, 2017, on [[Crackle (service)|Crackle]]. The series was created by [[Alex De Rakoff]] and stars [[Luke Pasqualino]], [[Rupert Grint]], [[Lucien Laviscount]], [[Phoebe Dynevor]], [[Juliet Aubrey]], [[Marc Warren]], [[Stephanie Leonidas]], [[Tamer Hassan]], and [[Dougray Scott]].

==Premise==
''Snatch'' follows a group of young [[scam]]mers who find themselves with a truck loaded with stolen [[gold bullion]] and are soon involved in the world of [[organized crime]].

==Cast and characters==
===Main===
* [[Luke Pasqualino]] as Albert Hill, a [[Cockney]] hustler
* [[Rupert Grint]] as Charlie Cavendish-Scott, Albert's partner in crime who comes from an aristocratic family
* [[Lucien Laviscount]] as Billy 'Fuckin' Ayres, a local half-[[Irish Traveller]] boxer and Albert and Charlie's friend
* [[Phoebe Dynevor]] as Lotti Mott, Sonny Castillo's [[Gun moll|moll]] who desperately wants out and decides to help Albert and Charlie in their scheme
* [[Juliet Aubrey]] as Lily Hill, Albert's mother
* [[Marc Warren]] as DI Bob Fink (season 1), a corrupt [[police inspector]] who operates as a local crime lord
* [[Stephanie Leonidas]] as Chloe Koen (season 1), a local gold dealer whom Charlie fancies
* [[Tamer Hassan]] as Hate 'Em, Vic's cellmate in prison
* [[Dougray Scott]] as Vic Hill, Albert's father, a legendary bank robber who still runs things from inside prison

==Production==
===Development===
On April 20, 2016, it was announced that [[Crackle (streaming service)|Crackle]] had given a series order to a television series adaptation of [[Guy Ritchie]]'s 2000 film ''[[Snatch (film)|Snatch]]'' for a first season consisting of ten episodes.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Stanhope |first1=Kate |title=Crackle Greenlights 'Snatch' Series Inspired by Guy Ritchie Film |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/crackle-greenlights-snatch-series-inspired-885987 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |accessdate=July 24, 2018 |language=en |date=April 20, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Spangler |first1=Todd |title=Crackle Greenlights 'Snatch' Drama Series Based on Guy Ritchie Movie |url=https://variety.com/2016/digital/news/crackle-snatch-drama-guy-ritchie-movie-1201757502/ |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |accessdate=July 24, 2018 |date=April 20, 2016}}</ref> On August 22, 2016, it was announced that the series was created by [[Alex De Rakoff]] who was also set to serve as the show's head writer and an executive producer. It was additionally announced that Helen Flint would act as a producer for the series, Nick Renton would direct, and that production companies involved with the series were expected to include Little Island Productions.<ref name="Grint">{{cite web |last1=Andreeva |first1=Nellie |title='Snatch': Rupert Grint To Star In Crackle Series Based On Guy Ritchie Movie |url=https://deadline.com/2016/08/snatch-rupert-grint-star-crackle-tv-series-remake-guy-ritchie-movie-1201806900/ |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |accessdate=July 24, 2018 |date=August 22, 2016}}</ref> 
Principal photography for season one was expected to commence during the week of August 29, 2016 in [[Manchester]], [[England]].<ref name="Grint"/>

On April 19, 2017, it was announced that Crackle had renewed the series for a second season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Andreeva |first1=Nellie |title=Crackle Orders 'The Oath' Drama Series Produced By 50 Cent & Movie 'In The Cloud', Renews 'Snatch' & 'SuperMansion' |url=https://deadline.com/2017/04/crackle-new-series-2016-2017-the-oath-snatch-1202072119/ |website=Deadline Hollywood |accessdate=July 24, 2018 |date=April 19, 2017}}</ref> On July 24, 2018, it was announced that season two would premiere on September 13, 2018.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rupert Grint Drama 'Snatch' Gets Season 2 Premiere Date On Sony Crackle |url=https://deadline.com/2018/07/rupert-grint-drama-snatch-returns-sony-crackle-sept-13-1202431938/ |website=Deadline Hollywood|accessdate=July 23, 2018 |date=July 23, 2018}}</ref>

===Casting===
In August 2016, it was announced that [[Rupert Grint]], [[Dougray Scott]], [[Luke Pasqualino]], and [[Lucien Laviscount]] had been cast in the series' lead roles and that [[Ed Westwick]] would appear in a recurring capacity.<ref name="Grint"/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Prudom |first1=Laura |title=Rupert Grint to Star in 'Snatch' Series from Crackle |url=https://variety.com/2016/tv/news/snatch-rupert-grint-ed-westwick-tv-show-crackle-1201842215/ |website=Variety |accessdate=July 24, 2018 |date=August 22, 2016}}</ref> On September 23, 2016, it was reported that [[Phoebe Dynevor]] had been cast in series regular role.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pedersen |first1=Erik |title=Phoebe Dynevor Joins Crackle's 'Snatch'; Jona Xiao Recurs On BET's 'Being Mary Jane' |url=https://deadline.com/2016/09/phoebe-dynevor-snatch-crackle-jona-xiao-being-mary-jane-1201825461/ |website=Deadline Hollywood |accessdate=July 24, 2018 |date=September 23, 2016}}</ref> On February 7, 2018, it was announced that [[Úrsula Corberó]] had been cast in a recurring role for the second season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Petski |first1=Denise |title=Allison Dunbar Joins Crackle's 'StartUp'; Úrsula Corberó In 'Snatch' |url=https://deadline.com/2018/02/allison-dunbar-crackle-startup-ursula-corbero-snatch-1202279880/ |website=Deadline Hollywood |accessdate=July 24, 2018 |date=February 7, 2018}}</ref>

==Release==
On January 13, 2017, the first trailer for the series was released.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lincoln |first1=Ross A. |title='Snatch' First Trailer: Lock, Stock And Two Crime Film Remakes? |url=https://deadline.com/2017/01/crackle-snatch-rupert-grint-first-trailer-1201885968/ |website=Deadline Hollywood |accessdate=July 24, 2018 |date=January 13, 2017}}</ref> On August 22, 2018, the official trailer for the second season was released.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Petski |first1=Denise |title='Snatch' Trailer: First Look At Season 2 Of Rupert Grint Sony Crackle Drama |url=https://deadline.com/2018/08/snatch-trailer-first-look-season-2-rupert-grint-sony-crackle-drama-1202450167/ |website=Deadline Hollywood |accessdate=August 22, 2018 |date=August 22, 2018}}</ref>

On March 9, 2017, the series held its world premiere at the ArcLight Culver City movie theater in [[Culver City, California]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Moskowitz |first1=Alana |title=Weasley Power! Rupert Grint and Bonnie Wright Reunite |url=https://www.eonline.com/news/835261/weasleys-forever-harry-potter-stars-rupert-grint-and-bonnie-wright-reunite-at-snatch-premiere |website=[[E!|E! Online]] |accessdate=July 24, 2018 |date=March 10, 2017}}</ref> On September 28, 2017, the series held its British premiere at the [[BT Tower]] in [[Fitzrovia]], [[London]], England.<ref name="UKPremiere">{{cite web |last1=Fletcher |first1=Alex |title=Watch a Facebook Live with Rupert Grint and the cast of Snatch |url=http://tv.bt.com/tv/amc-on-bt-tv/snatch-rupert-grint-luke-pasqualino-lucien-laviscount-facebook-live-11364216489788 |website=[[BT Group|BT]] |accessdate=July 24, 2018 |language=en |date=September 29, 2017}}</ref> On October 31, 2017, the series premiered on [[AMC (Europe)|AMC]] in the United Kingdom.<ref name="UKPremiere"/>

==Reception==
===Critical response===
The first season was met with a mixed to negative response from critics upon its debut. On the review aggregation website [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the series holds a 39% approval rating with an average rating of 4.80 out of 10 based on 18 reviews. The website's critical consensus reads, "''Snatch'' won't grab you."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/snatch/s01/ |title=Snatch: Season 1 |work=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |accessdate=July 24, 2018}}</ref> [[Metacritic]], which uses a weighted average, assigned the series a score of 55 out of 100 based on 9 critics, indicating "mixed or average reviews".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.metacritic.com/tv/snatch-2017 |title=Snatch: Season 1 |work=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |accessdate=May 14, 2019}}</ref>
